featured_reviews.name: Gurvinder Pal Singh Kalra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Title: A Refreshing Oasis in the Heart of Mumbai

As a resident of Mahim, I've been frequenting the Mahatma Gandhi Swimming Pool for many years, and I've always been impressed by its facilities and the overall swimming experience it offers. While there's always room for improvement, I believe the pool deserves a solid 4-star rating, reflecting its strengths and acknowledging the areas where it could enhance its offerings.

Cleanliness and Maintenance:

The pool complex is generally well-maintained, with clean and hygienic pools, changing rooms, and shower areas. The staff regularly checks the water quality, ensuring it meets the necessary standards. While there have been instances of minor cleanliness issues, they've been promptly addressed by the staff.

Facilities and Amenities:

The pool complex boasts a variety of amenities catering to swimmers of all ages and skill levels. The main pool, an Olympic-sized one, is ideal for lap swimming and training. The separate diving pool is perfect for practicing dives and aquatic stunts. Additionally, there's a smaller pool for kids, providing a safe and fun environment for them to learn and enjoy the water.

Pool Staff and Safety:

The pool staff is generally helpful and attentive, ensuring the safety of swimmers at all times. Experienced lifeguards are stationed around the pools, keeping a watchful eye on everyone. The pool also has clear signage and safety guidelines in place to minimize the risk of accidents.

Overall Experience:

Mahatma Gandhi Swimming Pool is a great place to come for a refreshing swim, whether you're looking for a leisurely workout or a fun family outing. The pool's facilities are well-maintained, the staff is friendly and helpful, and the safety measures are commendable. While there's always room for improvement, the pool consistently delivers a positive swimming experience, earning it a solid 4-star rating.

Areas for Improvement:

Parking: The pool's parking facilities can be limited during peak hours, making it challenging to find a spot. Expanding the parking area or introducing valet parking services would be beneficial.

Shower Rooms: The shower rooms could be refurbished to provide a more modern and comfortable experience. Upgrading the fixtures and adding more shower cubicles would enhance the overall experience.

Food Options: While there are a few snack and beverage options available at the canteen it closes by 9 pm and expanding the food menu to include more substantial meals would cater to swimmers who spend longer hours at the pool.

Despite these areas for improvement, Mahatma Gandhi Swimming Pool remains a valuable asset to the Dadar community and a popular choice for both casual swimmers and fitness enthusiasts. Its dedication to cleanliness, safety, and providing a welcoming environment makes it a rewarding place to spend a day in the water.

featured_reviews.name: anL
featured_reviews.review_text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but after months of seeing the same problems and hearing the same complaints from other members, I feel this needs to be said.

The condition of this pool is simply unacceptable. Almost every time I visit, there are visible particles, bugs, slimy debris, and other contaminants floating in the water. The pool frequently looks dirty, and the filtration system rarely appears to be running. On one recent visit, the water was so dirty that I swam for barely two minutes before getting out and calling staff to inspect it. Instead of acknowledging the issue, I was told the pool was clean while visible debris remained in the water.

The area around the pool is no better. Rats, pigeons, and large insects are commonly seen around the facility, and there have been occasions where what appeared to be rat droppings were present near one of the staircases. For any swimming facility, this should be treated as a serious hygiene issue, not something that is repeatedly ignored.

The washrooms are honestly shocking. They often have a very strong smell, zero ventilation, and become unbearably hot. There is not even a fan in the bathroom area, making it feel like a sauna. The shower water pressure is so weak that it is barely usable. When concerns about the smell were raised, the response was essentially that it was “mostly the men’s washroom,” which completely misses the point. Members should not have to deal with that in the first place.

Maintenance across the facility appears to be severely neglected. Multiple tiles under the pool are cracked, the handrail used to enter the pool shakes and feels loose, and other damaged handrails seem to stay broken for months without repair. These are basic safety issues that should have been addressed long ago.

Another incident that I found highly unprofessional involved a female staff member sitting in the shower area wrapped only in a towel and appearing ready to use the same shower facilities as members. Regardless of the circumstances, this reflected poorly on the professionalism and management of the facility.

What is most frustrating is that these problems are not new. Virtually every regular member I have spoken to has complained about the same issues. The standard response is always “we’ll check” or “we’ll look into it,” yet nothing ever seems to change. Members are even told to come at different times if the pool is dirty, which is unreasonable. If the facility opens at 7:00 AM, the pool should be clean and ready to use at 7:00 AM—not hours later.

There is also often no visible attendant, maintenance staff member, or lifeguard around the pool area. For a facility charging members and operating a swimming pool, the lack of supervision is concerning.

At this point, the issue is not a dirty day or a one-off maintenance problem. It is a pattern of poor cleanliness, poor upkeep, and a management team that seems far more interested in dismissing complaints than fixing them. This facility has potential, but potential means very little when the same problems continue month after month despite repeated complaints from members.

There are far better-maintained pools in the area that take cleanliness, safety, and member concerns seriously. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this facility.

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Positives:

Temperature-Controlled Pool – A big advantage, especially during rains and winter.
9-Foot Depth – Ideal for learning diving and improving treading water skills.
6-Day Availability – Open six days a week, making it easy to choose batches as per convenience.
Coaches – Highly professional, patient, courteous, dedicated, and knowledgeable.
All Swimming Strokes – Comprehensive training covering freestyle, breaststroke, backstroke, and butterfly.
Patient Learning Approach – Coaches ensure everyone learns at their own pace with proper attention.
Supportive Staff – Mouzam, Sakshi, and the entire administrative team are extremely helpful and cooperative.
All Age Groups Welcome – From kids as young as 5 to adults over 75, proving age is never a barrier.

My Journey:

I already knew breaststroke, but I always wanted to learn the other swimming styles. Like many, I never really found the time or push to start. When my wife joined the Michael Phelps Swimming program at Willingdon Sports Club, I would accompany her. One day, Mouzam encouraged me to join as well.

Initially, I was unsure—did I really need to learn new strokes? But I eventually decided to take the plunge, both literally and figuratively.

Starting out wasn’t easy. Learning new strokes felt challenging, but beginner coach Mahesh Sir played a key role in helping me pick up freestyle and backstroke. As I progressed, advanced coach Prayag Sir helped refine my breaststroke—I realized how much energy I had been wasting due to incorrect technique. He also guided me through learning butterfly, which is by far the most challenging stroke. Along the way, he fine-tuned all my strokes, especially backstroke and breaststroke.

Both coaches offered exceptional guidance, focusing on technique, form correction, drills, and personalized attention.

A special mention to Sameer Sir as well—though I had limited sessions with him, his professionalism and dedication stood out.

Even with prior knowledge of basic swimming, it took me nearly a year to confidently learn all strokes. The coaches and staff are incredibly friendly and always ready to help with any concerns.

A big thank you to Mahesh Sir, Prayag Sir, and Mouzam for their consistent support and dedication.

Final Thought:
The facility and coaching are excellent—but consistency is the key to truly learning and improving in swimming.

featured_reviews.name: Ryan Rodricks
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently completely refurbished and opened back to the general public.

Pool - 50 Metre Olympic spec. size with starting boards and lane markings (underwater).
Max depth- 17 Feet
Minimum Depth - 4 Feet
Lanes - 10
Access ladders - 6

The pool itself is very very good. The water is clean, minimal chlorine and no skin infections or rashes like you sometimes get with dirty water. The water filters seem to be working effectively.
Rules
Only swimers allowed onto the swim area level and around the pool.
Swimming costume is compulsory.

The facilities are well maintained, the staff are helpful and the overall experience is very good.

Timings
Morning 06.00am to 11.00am
Ladies 11.00am to 12.00pm

Evening 06.00pm to 10.00pm
Ladies 05.00 to 06.00pm

Overall Swimming Experience - 3/5

The Swimming experience itself is quite a mess. Filled with senior citizens/ middle-aged aged men with absolutely no sense of how a swimming pool works.
This is comparable to Mumbai traffic but in water.
People swim in any direction, breadth wise, diagonal wise, criss-crossing from anywhere and just getting into each other's way. There is absolutely no concept of swimming in a 50M pool and the crowd is comparable to a Waterpark on weekends.

If you're a casual swimmer just looking to get wet on a hot summers day then it's perfect.

If you're a professional swimmer looking to put in some practice laps when not coaching, then you will be disappointed.

It's impossible to actually swim 50M uninterrupted. Whatever the batch time.

The BMC should allocate a set timing slot morning/evening for serious swimmers only. Easier said than done though as its a common pool and arguments are bound to arise.

Overall the facilities are very good and the experience is nice but for competition level swimmers looking for extra practice it's not worth the time.

featured_reviews.name: Vasanth Pragash
featured_reviews.review_text:
November 2025 review

Pool is big and possibly olympic size. The pool has various depths starting from shallow end of 4 feet to over 15 feet depth. The pool is trifurcated into three areas, 1) Shallow end ,2) 2 Full length lanes( this reduces the width of the pool for the other 2) 3) Main pool area. Small lockers, shower rooms etc are available at no extra cost.

Membership process:
Full the details online in the website, be sure to upload aadhaar and pay the amount. For verification you will need aadhaar copy, printout of 2 receipts(one will become your id), original copy of doctors medical certificate stating you have no skin diseases or communicable diseases and are fit to swim, and three passport photos.They will take aadhaar copy, both receipt copies,the doctors medical certificate and photos. You will recive an SMS that registration is done and they will give you back one stamped receipt with your photo as your medical id. Laminate it or keep it in a ziplock bag.

Advantages:
1) Very friendly staff. They are extremely courteous and helpful in resolving pool queries and so on.
2) Very convenient timings. 6AM-12 noon (11-12 ladies only) and 5-10PM (5-6PM ladies only)
3) Pool is maintained very clean despite its public nature.

Disadvantages:
1) Nothing is provided, no soap, towels or paper.
2) You will need to bring your own locks, lockers are very small so make sure you buy a small lock.
3) Restrictions apply on swimwear , no full body suits for anyone and men can only wear swim shorts. No cotton shorts, etc allowed. If you come in morning you can buy swimming shorts, goggles and swim caps from the reception but it could be expensive.
4) Pool is extremely clorinated, and you can feel it in your teeth and hair. Be sure to brush and clean yourself as soon as your done with swimming. No shower doors for showers.
5) This is a public pool, which means a lot of people will be using it, this is understandable but can cause problems if your trying to swim laps as many kids/adults will crash your path. If this is the case stick to pool area 2).

Best time to swim would be 9-11 in the morning as a guy, most people are working and the sun is bright such that the pool isn't too cold.
